title.narrative: NFI and shelter emergency assistance to IDP households in Bangadi victims of LRA attacks in Dungu

description.narrative:
Bangadi is situated in North East DRC in Dungu Diocese, Haut Uélé District, Oriental Province. It is 75 kms south of Sudan. Bangadi and surrounding villages have been attacked severally by the LRAs causing the people from these villages flee to Bangadi for safety. Bangadi itself was attacked twice in 2008 and 2009 but has remained under threat of LRA attacks for months. As a coping defence mechanism, the local population formed local self defence groups to protect the population against potential LRA attacks. Currently Bangadi is home to 26559 inhabitants of which 11558 persons are IDPs. These LRA attacks begun in Mbamu-Limolo village in August 25th, Kana village September 2nd, Napopo October 12th.
LRA attacks caused a lot of problems such as the destruction of property, looting, killing, abduction of children, men and women, rape, torching of houses and massive displacement of the population in different direction externally towards South Sudan into Yambio Diocese and internally to Niangara, Dungu, Isiro and Ngilima. In Bangadi itself a small minority of the population braved the attacks and decided not to leave and it is this population that hosted IDPs from Diagbe, Doruma, Kapili, Banda and Niangara. The humanitarian situation in Bangadi remained alarming as there has been no assistance to this area due to lack of accessibility exacerbated by the insecurity caused by the presence of LRAs along the roads leading to Bangadi. This insecurity caused a lot of protection concerns as bringing aid to Bangadi while the LRAs are hovering around would have been going against the DO NO HARM principle. Currently there is enough security in Bangadi because of the deployment of the FARDC in and around Bangadi. This situation though doesn’t give enough guarantee to the IDPs to return to their homes. This security offers humanitarian agencies the opportunity to bring assistance to Bangadi without increasing any vulnerability to the beneficiaries in particular and the entire community in general. Caritas Dungu is planning to bring in NFI/Shelter assistance to these IDPs made up of blankets, soap, Jerri cans, sleeping mats, mosquito nets, clothing and tarpaulins. Other needs will be covered for by other agencies such as MSF, and Medair. Caritas who is also a partner with the WFP is also preparing to contact them and request them for food.
